speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a history suggestive of bone fragility and unusual physical features; can you describe your childhood fractures and any specific facial or skeletal abnormalities you've noticed? Also, how old are you and at what age did your mother experience menarche?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH) due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth (clitoromegaly, partial labial fusion), delayed menarche, severe acne, and history of fractures in an adolescent female is highly suggestive of this condition. I need to confirm if you have experienced rapid growth spurts or short stature compared to your parents, and I will request a 17-hydroxyprogesterone level test.
